narrative.t: Between 18 Jun 2026 and 28 Oct 2026 (NISAR, 10 passes, track 056 ascending), the open water in the box (sea or a large lake running past the box edge) shrank from 372 km² on 18 Jun to 20.2 km² on 28 Oct, mostly between 30 Jun and 28 Oct, after peaking at 445 km² on 30 Jun (all water-dark pixels in the box: 375 → 20.2 km²). Careful: open water jumps like this when wind roughens it and it turns radar-bright, so this is more likely weather than a real shoreline change.
narrative.s: Water-dark = smoothed brightness below 91 of 255 (Otsu split in the 18 Jun histogram); main body = largest connected dark patch, 465 km² at its widest

narrative.t: On the map, 351 km² that was water-dark on 18 Jun no longer is by 28 Oct (orange, "water lost": drying shore), and 0.00 km² became water-dark (blue, "water gained").
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 18 Jun vs 28 Oct 2026; same water threshold, first vs last pass, only within 300 m of the dark water bodies

narrative.t: Across the whole box, 0.75 km² became much darker in radar (new water, wetter or smoother ground) and 0.00 km² became much brighter (rougher or bare ground, structures, debris or crops).
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 18 Jun vs 28 Oct 2026; more than 4 robust σ (47 of 255 levels) after 5×5 smoothing; 0.48 km² on steep, shadowed terrain left out

narrative.t: The largest single patch (marker 1) is 280 km² of water lost, around 25.120° N, 55.085° E (brightness 76 → 119 of 255).
416 km² jumped by more than 4× its own normal pass-to-pass wobble, most of it (361 km²) between 16 Oct and 28 Oct; the same test on the first pair flags 164 km², a rough false-alarm level.
narrative.s: Per-pixel temporal anomaly over 10 passes (median absolute successive difference)

narrative.t: The plant signal (HV-like green channel) rose by 5% across the box, consistent with more vegetation or rougher surfaces.
Grouping pixels that behave alike over time gives 6 zones; none changes strongly as a whole, and the "dark all season" zone (likely open water) covers 203 km².
narrative.s: Unsupervised k-means on per-pixel time profiles; labels are interpretations

narrative.t: NASA EONET lists floods "Flood in Lithuania 1104069" on 31 Jul; USGS lists no M4+ earthquakes within about 50 km of this box in this period. That is context, not proof of cause.
narrative.s: NASA EONET v3 and USGS FDSN event APIs, box ± 0.5°
